clue.text: Amazed and totally lost for words

definitions.meaning: first meaning: so astonished as to be unable to talk
second meaning: literally without any speech at all

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves describe someone struck dumb; the second is the literal sense, the first the figurative one.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stunned into silence and being entirely unable to talk are both described by this single adjective.

clue.text: Might such an entrance catch one unawares?

definitions.text: Might such an entrance catch one unawares?

parts.words: Might such an entrance catch one unawares?
parts.note: surface reading: a doorway that surprises someone coming through it
setter's reading: a hinged hatch in a floor or stage that can drop a person who steps on it, like a snare

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a particular doorway could take a visitor by surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch' suggests surprise, but the joke is that the entrance is literally a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged panel set into a floor or ceiling is an entrance, and its name contains a snare for catching prey.

clue.text: A very noisy chap joined in a brawl

parts.note: ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud
Ray is a man's name, so any chap

explanation.surface: A loud man got involved in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: In music ff (fortissimo) marks a passage to be played very loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: An affray is a public fight or disturbance, a legal term for a brawl in a public place.

clue.text: Aspersion cast by thoughtless, lurid piece

indicators.note: a piece is a fragment cut from something longer, so the letters are a run taken from the words before it

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: An insult is thrown out by a careless, sensational article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like part of the definition (aspersions are cast), and it is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A slur is a damaging remark against someone's reputation, the same thing as an aspersion.

clue.text: True proofs about a place to sleep

indicators.note: about suggests letters moved around in every direction, a scrambling of their order

explanation.surface: Genuine printed proofs concerning somewhere to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-poster is a large bed with a post at each corner, so it is somewhere one sleeps.

clue.text: Stage scenery for group work

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a freestanding piece of theatre scenery
second meaning: a rehearsed team move, as at a football corner or free kick

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one theatre job, scenery built by a team; the two phrases are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre the phrase names a standalone scenic construction; in sport it names a planned team routine from a dead ball.

clue.text: US code used legal tender once

indicators.note: used in the sense of worn or knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American legal code was applied to what used to count as money.
explanation.definitionFit: The escudo was Portugal's currency until the euro replaced it, so it was formerly accepted money.

clue.text: Student leaves reply about heap of wood for burning

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the remaining letters are rearranged
when someone leaves they are no longer present, so that letter goes

parts.note: L is the learner plate, standing for a student

explanation.surface: A student walks off from an answer about a bonfire.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove L from REPLY to get REPY, then rearrange. L for learner comes from the L-plates on UK learner drivers' cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A pyre is a pile of combustible material, especially one built for cremating a body.

clue.text: Case of wine one fool damaged

indicators.note: something damaged is broken out of shape, so these letters are reformed

explanation.surface: A crate of wine was broken by some idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case of wine' reads as one phrase, but Case is the definition and wine starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A portfolio is a flat carrying case for papers or drawings.

clue.text: Attempt easy trip round Sweden

indicators.note: to trip is to stumble, so the letters fall out of order
the rearranged word goes round another letter, enclosing it

parts.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: Someone tries a gentle holiday touring Sweden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Easy trip' reads as a relaxing journey; trip is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay, as a noun, is a try at doing something, an older sense still used formally.

clue.text: Leading female soloist reportedly leaving performers playing Beethoven's 5th

indicators.note: playing suggests fooling about, so the remaining letters are rearranged
letters leaving a word depart from it and are taken out
the leading part of each of the next three words is its opening letter

parts.note: the initial letter of each word

explanation.surface: A prima donna, it is said, walks out on musicians performing a Beethoven symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a diva and the Fifth Symphony; 'reportedly' looks like a sound signal but just supplies its first letter. Taking F, S, R from PERFORMERS leaves PEROMER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Emperor is the popular nickname of Beethoven's Piano Concerto No 5, so it is his fifth concerto.

clue.text: Break up: truer version

indicators.note: a version is a different rendering of something, so the letters are recast

explanation.surface: A note on splitting up says it gives a more honest account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break up' reads as a phrasal verb, but only Break is the definition; up is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A rupture is a breach or split, whether in a pipe, a tissue or a relationship.

clue.text: Nonsense call for attention without spectacles

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word stands on the outside of the other

parts.note: hey is a shout to get someone to notice
two round lenses look like a pair of Os

explanation.surface: A shouted plea for notice from someone who has left their glasses behind is rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it keeps its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooey is informal American slang for silly talk or rubbish.

clue.text: Keep in reserve with space in the larder, say

parts.note: to store is to keep for later

explanation.surface: Put food by, using the free shelves in the pantry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks the larder as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A larder is a cool room for keeping food, one kind of room used for storing supplies.

clue.text: Young friend to train lively team

parts.note: to school someone is to train or teach them

indicators.note: lively suggests jumping about, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young pal is going to coach an energetic side.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmate is a fellow pupil, someone young who is a friend from the same school.

clue.text: Large wine bottle and spilt soup presented as a great work of art

parts.note: a magnum holds two ordinary bottles of wine

indicators.note: something spilt is splashed out of its container, so these letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A big bottle of wine and some upset soup are passed off as a masterpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: The scene suggests a messy still life or conceptual installation.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnum opus is Latin for great work, used of the most important creation of an artist or writer.

clue.text: Gatherers hint at broadcast that's phenomenal

indicators.note: broadcast in its old farming sense of seed scattered widely, so these letters are strewn about

explanation.surface: Collectors suggest a remarkable programme on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' fits the gatherers' farming picture as sowing, and that scattering is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something earth-shattering is so momentous or extraordinary it seems to shake the world.

clue.text: Deer Tom's treated was definitely the last

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase; the answer means furthest back

parts.note: a hind is a female deer

indicators.note: something treated has been processed or altered, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: The deer that Tom looked after came in well behind everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: Known from the saying 'the devil take the hindmost', about whoever lags farthest behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindmost means furthest to the rear, so the one plainly at the very back of a group.

clue.text: Hire sis a building on a large stretch of water

indicators.note: building means constructing something new, so these letters are assembled into another order

explanation.surface: Rent your sister a house on the edge of a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The Irish Sea lies between Great Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish Sea is a broad body of seawater separating Ireland from Britain.

clue.text: Show way to spend our pound inside

indicators.note: inside places one letter within the phrase before it

parts.note: L, from Latin libra, is the symbol for a pound

explanation.surface: Instructions on how to use up our cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' reads as money to be spent, but it gives only the letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendour is magnificent display, the grand show of a pageant or palace.

clue.text: Survive former lover turning up in the most easy-going way

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; read 'in the most easy-going way' loosely as laxest

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
in a down entry, turning up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Getting through an awkward reunion with an old flame by being as relaxed as possible.
explanation.definitionFit: Lax means slack or not strict, so laxest is the least strict or most permissive of all.

clue.text: Aide ordered you, say, to bid farewell

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new sequence, so these letters are rearranged
say asks for a letter that is pronounced like the word before it

parts.note: the letter U is pronounced like this pronoun

explanation.surface: An assistant told you to say goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is French for goodbye, borrowed into English as a formal parting word.

clue.text: Maid lost on street at the Centre

indicators.note: something lost has gone astray, so these letters wander out of order

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A servant has got lost on a road in the middle of town.
explanation.definitionFit: Amidst is a preposition meaning in the middle of, so surrounded at the core by something.

clue.text: Top of the range for very large parent?

parts.note: maxi means extra large, as in a maxi skirt
Mum is the British word for mother

explanation.surface: A best-of-the-line product suited to a very big mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top of the range' reads as a luxury product, but here means the highest point of a scale.
explanation.definitionFit: A maximum is the greatest value reached, the upper limit of any span of values.

clue.text: Dumb letter to Greece by Lawrence

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet
T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia

explanation.surface: A foolish letter sent to Greece from Lawrence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter to Greece' reads as post, but means a letter belonging to the Greek alphabet; 'by' just places one piece beside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumb in its older sense means unable to speak, which is exactly what mute describes.

clue.text: Sigh when High Horse waywardly runs outsiders off

indicators.note: waywardly means going astray, so the letters are rearranged
off means removed, so those letters are taken away
the outsiders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone sighs as a stallion called High Horse bolts off course.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking R and S from HIGHHORSE leaves HIGHHOE to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Heigh-ho is an exclamation of weary resignation, the verbal equivalent of a sigh.

clue.text: Animal's foot had one of five to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with points at how each word starts, so the opening letters are taken

parts.note: initial letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: An animal's foot had one of its five toes at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoof is the horny covering on the foot of a horse, cow or similar beast.

clue.text: A thousand thanks when coming round for work

indicators.note: coming round describes one word wrapping itself about the other

parts.note: a written short form of thanks, its K standing for a thousand
as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Huge gratitude whenever someone drops by to help out.
explanation.walkthrough: TKS is a shorthand for thanks; the setter folds in 'A thousand' because K is the usual abbreviation for a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasks are pieces of work to be done, jobs assigned to someone.

clue.text: The first French painter to produce things for a bride

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: Henri Rousseau, the French naive painter of jungle scenes

explanation.surface: The leading French artist makes gifts for a bride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The first French painter' reads as one title; split it so The gives its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A trousseau is the clothes, linen and household goods a bride collects for her marriage.
